transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Menon (CISO, Peninsula Health), Aisha Khan (IT Ops), Tom Reed (Head of Data), Maya Singh (Privacy Lead), Ben Cole (Procurement), Sanjay Patel (DevOps)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick around the room -- I'm Lena from Redwood, and Marcus our solutions engineer is with me.
[00:18] Priya: Hi Lena, thanks. I'm Priya, CISO at Peninsula Health. we want to understand security posture for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and specifically how you handle SOC2, SSO, encryption, retention.
[00:35] Marcus: great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. we'll do a high-level then dive into the specifics you listed. feel free to interrupt.
[00:42] Aisha: quick note: we are a hybrid cloud shop, majority of patient data is in our AWS VPC in us-east-1, but we have EU tenancy for research. data residency is a big one.
[01:00] Lena: noted. first question - are you planning to send any PHI through Redwood Hosted, or is the plan Dedicated/Private only?
[01:10] Tom: good question. our immediate goal is to prototype with de-identified notes on Hosted, but long term we expect PHI workloads and will likely need Dedicated or Private.
[01:25] Maya: compliance requires SOC2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 if possible; we also have internal questionnaire and a list of encryption/KMS requirements.
[01:36] Marcus: for SOC2 we can share our Type II report and control matrix. Redwood Hosted is SOC2 Type II, and for Dedicated/Private customers we provide additional isolation and can support SOC 2-related attestations within contracts.
[01:50] Priya: do you have ISO 27001 accreditation?
[01:55] Lena: we don't currently carry ISO 27001, we prioritize SOC2 for the hosted platform and for enterprise we provide tailored controls and audit support. we can share our gap remediation plan and third-party penetration test results.
[02:12] Ben: on encryption - what's at-rest and in-flight? customer-managed keys?
[02:17] Marcus: all traffic is TLS in transit. at rest, hosted uses provider-managed keys by default; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or similar). you can bring your own key and rotate as needed.
[02:36] Sanjay: can we revoke keys in the event of a compromise quickly, and will sessions using old tokens invalidate?
[02:42] Marcus: yes, with BYOK you control key rotation and revocation. for sessions, our runtime checks access tokens - revoking keys would prevent future decrypt operations, but in-flight session behaviour is something we'd coordinate in the pilot.
[02:58] Aisha: audit logs - what granularity do you capture? who has access, and retention windows?
[03:06] Marcus: we capture admin actions, API calls, model selection, user id (where provided), and token-level usage for billing/forensics. logs can be streamed to your SIEM via webhook or forwarded to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Stackdriver) for Dedicated/Private. retention policy is configurable; Hosted default is 90 days for detailed traces, 365 days for aggregated metrics, but enterprise packages can extend retention or export to your storage for long-term archival.
[03:38] Maya: we need immutable audit logs for at least 7 years for some records; is that supported?
[03:45] Lena: yes - for Dedicated/Private we can set up long-term archival to your S3/GCS with WORM-style retention via your storage config. we'll document recommended architecture.
[03:55] Priya: SSO - do you support SAML? SCIM provisioning?
[03:59] Marcus: yes. Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is available in the Console - you can map SAML attributes to roles and onboard via SCIM. for Private deployments you can also integrate with your IdP via VPN or peered connectivity.
[04:18] Tom: does RBAC cover model-level permissions? e.g., restrict who can call certain model routes or view logs?
[04:24] Marcus: we have role constructs: admin, developer, auditor, billing. you can also create route-level policies and tag models/environments. auditors get read-only log access; developers get deploy/run privileges; admins manage keys and network.
[04:40] Priya: do you provide a read-only view for our SOC team to pull evidence?
[04:45] Lena: yes we can set up auditor roles and provide exports of logs and config states. we also provide signed attestation artifacts and can enable API access for automated evidence collection.
[04:58] Maya: data retention & deletion - if a user requests deletion, how is that and how quickly?
[05:05] Marcus: we support API and console-based deletion requests. for Hosted, we have data retention defaults and can delete customer data on request - typical propagation is within 30 days but we'll provide contractual SLAs for Dedicated/Private. for PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the storage lifecycle.
[05:26] Aisha: any managed backups or snapshots that could retain data beyond deletion?
[05:30] Marcus: snapshots exist for operational recovery; for Dedicated we can configure backup retention to meet your policy and ensure backups are encrypted with your KMS. deletion workflows include snapshot pruning.
[05:46] Ben: procurement question: what about contractual terms - can you agree to custom security addenda and audit rights?
[05:52] Lena: yes, for enterprise deals we commonly include security addenda, right to audit clauses (with notice), and tailored SLAs. we'll share a template MSA and security addendum.
[06:05] Priya: network isolation - for Dedicated, are instances in our VPC or co-located?
[06:10] Marcus: Dedicated runs in logically isolated pools within our cloud accounts but we support VPC peering, PrivateLink, or customer VPC connectors depending on cloud. for fully isolated on-prem we offer Private deployment.
[06:25] Sanjay: performance question: if we run a pilot with PHI on Dedicated, can we test throughput and latency and produce profiling?
[06:33] Marcus: absolutely - part of the POC we run benchmarks with your typical prompt distributions, sequence lengths and we instrument latency/throughput and token cost. we'll include KV cache profiling and batching recommendations.
[06:48] Priya: I heard about model fallbacks and caching - if there's a redirection to a cheaper variant, how do we ensure compliance with our policy?
[06:56] Lena: routing policies are configurable per-customer; you can disable fallback or restrict to approved model families. we capture all routing decisions in logs for audit.
[07:10] Tom: regarding data residency - we need processing in EU for certain datasets. how do you guarantee that?
[07:17] Marcus: we can pin workloads to specific regions and avoid cross-region routing. for Hosted we have region-specific endpoints; Dedicated/Private gives you more controls and an option to deploy in your region of choice.
[07:33] Maya: what about penetration testing and vuln disclosure?
[07:36] Lena: we run regular third-party pentests and have a vulnerability disclosure policy. we can share summary reports and coordinate a joint testing plan for enterprise customers under NDA.
[07:50] Aisha: what are typical timelines to go from discovery to Dedicated pilot?
[07:54] Marcus: typically 2-4 weeks to spin up a small Dedicated pool and configure network/SSO, then a 2-week pilot. depends on procurement and any legal/contract negotiations.
[08:06] Ben: procurement will need pricing and E2E security docs before legal signs off.
[08:10] Lena: we'll send pricing for Dedicated pilot, our SOC2 report, security deck, and the MSA template.
[08:16] Priya: one more - how do you handle privacy & data minimization? are prompts/logs truncated or hashed?
[08:24] Marcus: we offer options: redaction at ingestion, prompt minimization patterns, and you can configure telemetry to avoid storing raw prompts. we also support tokenization or client-side preprocessing.
[08:40] Maya: we will run the security questionnaire now and follow up with detailed answers; want to confirm who to send it to.
[08:47] Lena: send to me and cc Marcus and I'll get our security team to triage.
[08:53] Aisha: timeline - we aim to have a vendor selected by end of Q2.
[08:57] Lena: that's doable. we'll prioritize the artifacts.
[09:03] Marcus: quick recap of technical commitments - BYOK for KMS, SAML + SCIM, configurable audit retention, log forwarding to SIEM, region pinning, and pilot performance profiling.
[09:18] Lena: next steps recap: I'll send SOC2 + security deck and MSA template; Marcus will schedule the SE deep dive and pilot scoping; Peninsula team will return questionnaire and network diagram.
[09:31] Priya: thanks everyone. that covers it for us.
[09:35] Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and schedule the deep dive.
